To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the direction-selective circuitry in the retina is more complicated and diverse than previously thought.

1) the direction-selective response of retinal ganglion cells depends on the temporal asymmetries arising from the differential connections of cholinergic versus GABAergic starburst amacrinic cells to ganglion cells and 2) the direction-selectivity of ganglion cells is refined by two distinct mechanisms, both arising in the starburst amacrine network.
Direction-selectivity is generated in the retina through a mechanism involving both asymmetric inhibition and excitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the cellular basis of direction selectivity, a fundamental property of visual motion processing in the vertebrate retina.
the mechanisms that generate direction-selective responses in retinal ganglion cells.
the cellular mechanisms of direction selectivity in mammalian vision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

starburst cells are not necessary for directional selectivity, but that their dendritic morphology is essential for the precise temporal pattern of excitation and inhibition that determines direction selectivity.
the direction selectivity of ganglion cells is generated by two mechanisms that arise from the differential connectivity pattern of the starburst cells.
the starburst cells provide the necessary and sufficient conditions for generating direction selectivity in ganglion cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

direction selectivity is not an all-or-none phenomenon, but instead is shaped by two core mechanisms, both arising in the starburst network, which work in concert to generate the precise spatiotemoral patterns of inhibition/excitation that determine directionality in downstream ganglion cell responses.
direction selectivity is a property of the starburst amacrine network, not a property of the dendrites of starburst cells.
direction selectivity is a robust property of ganglion cell receptive fields and that this property is shaped by two core mechanisms, both arising in the starburst amacrine network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
direction selectivity is not a property that is uniquely encoded in starburst dendrites, as it can be maintained when these dendrites are made non-directional.
direction selectivity arises from a complex network of mechanisms that operate in a highly coordinated way.
, although the direction-selectivity of starburst amacrine dendrites is necessary for direction-selectivity in downstream ganglia, it is not sufficient.
